claims.claim: BigBird sparse attention mechanism (random + window + global tokens) whose complexity is linear in sequence length
claims.quote: To remedy this, we propose, B IG B IRD, a sparse attention mechanism that reduces this quadratic dependency to linear.
claims.ablation_quote: We found that random blocks and local window were insufficient in capturing all the context necessary to compete with the performance of BERT.

claims.claim: Global tokens (ITC/ETC) attending to the entire sequence are critical for expressivity and performance
claims.quote: our theoretical analysis reveals some of the benefits of having O(1) global tokens (such as CLS), that attend to the entire sequence as part of the sparse attention mechanism.

claims.claim: BigBird is a universal approximator of sequence functions and Turing complete
claims.quote: We show that B IG B IRD is a universal approximator of sequence functions and is Turing complete, thereby preserving these properties of the quadratic, full attention model.

claims.claim: Handles sequences up to 8x longer than previously possible on similar hardware
claims.quote: The proposed sparse attention can handle sequences of length up to 8x of what was previously possible using similar hardware.

claims.claim: State-of-the-art results on question answering and document summarization
claims.quote: We achieve state of the art results for question answering and document summarization on a number of different datasets.

claims.claim: Novel application of attention models to genomics sequences (DNA) with long-context MLM pretraining
claims.quote: Lastly, we introduce a novel application of attention based models where long contexts are beneficial: extracting contextual representations of genomics sequences like DNA.

seeds.quote: Experiments on smaller IMDb and Hyperpartisan datasets are repeated 5 times and the average performance is presented along with standard deviation.

scores_copied.quote: The Test results (F1 for HotpotQA, Natural Questions, TriviaQA, and Accuracy for WikiHop) have been picked from their respective leaderboard.

third_party.quote: In Tab. 3, we compare B IG B IRD-ETC model to top-3 entries from the leaderboard excluding B IG B IRD.

data_disclosure.quote: We use four publicly available datasets Books [110], CC-News [34], Stories [89] and Wikipedia to pretrain B IG B IRD.

coding.note: Method-style paper, but the authors pretrain and release base/large BigBird models with code, so it is coded as a release report. Table 1 compares building blocks (R, W, R+W vs BERT) at length 512, but there is no with/without-global ablation, so the sparse-attention claim is PARTIAL and the global-token claim is NO. Data is coded PARTIAL rather than FULL: Table 9 gives sources and dataset token counts, but sampling proportions are not given and training warm-starts from RoBERTa. Tokens trained on and NLP training duration are not stated; only TPU slice sizes are given, so tokens and compute are both N. Rerun/scores are MIXED: Table 3 scores come from leaderboards, while Pegasus was re-evaluated by the authors. The Pegasus rerun quote is taken from a table row, so it may fail verbatim matching if spacing differs.
